name: Leg press
cue: Keep your lower back on the pad and drive through your heels.
research: research.json biomech.leg_press: back pad 30 deg above horizontal (trunk -60), 45 deg sled, plate perpendicular to the rails, feet high at ~50 cm stance, toes out 10 deg; hip 128 -> 90, knee 80 -> 10, ankle 27 -> -5, abduction 15 -> 10; closed chain hip - knee + ankle = 75. The rig limits hip flexion to 122 and ankle dorsiflexion to 28, so on the closed chain the knee can reach at most ~75: depth is hip 119, knee 71, ankle 27, inside the research band and under the rig limit (the research view note asks for hip under about 110-115 with the pelvis flat; the rig pelvis is rigid, so it stays flat on the pad). Lockout knee 10 with the hip (86.03) solved so the foot moves on the 45 deg rail line; sled travel 0.16 m. Soles held flat on the sliding plate by foot IK. Hands: the research grip (side handles by the seat, shoulder abduction 20, elbow 20) lays the forearm across the lateral hip, over the working glutes and quads from the side camera, so the handles sit on the pad frame level with the front of the pelvis instead (shoulder extension ~40, abduction ~28, elbow ~100, elbows back beside the pad); arm angles are not targeted. Seat pan under the pelvis rising 12 deg toward the front; the sit bones rest on it. The skin is bound at the stretched pose (motion.bind 0.074 s into the press), which paints the glute and vastus lateralis footprints so they meet in a broad band at every hip angle. Muscles: research primaries glute max and vastus lateralis glow (the vastus medialis faces away on the near leg and only the far leg's showed, as a detached patch by the knee, so it is not drawn); rectus femoris (research secondary, slack at this hip flexion) stays dark because it borders the vasti, and the adductor magnus (research primary for the feet-high press) lies on the inner thigh, which faces away from the side camera on the near leg and is hidden behind it on the far leg, so it is not drawn and has no chip. Head: a headrest continues the back pad so the head lies on it with a neutral neck (neck 2, head 0) instead of craning forward off the pad end. Geometry: tools/design/leg_press.mjs. Load: plate horns on the sled carriage (the plates ride up the rails with the sled). (tools/design/loads.mjs)

targets.note: depth: the research biomech entry gives hip 128 / knee 80; the rig limits hip flexion to 122 and the closed chain (ankle <= 28) caps the knee, so depth is hip 119 / knee 71 (the researched 18 deg shin), inside the standard tolerance

camera.note: Research view az 90 / el 10, unchanged: the glutes and vasti face the side camera at every phase, and the horizon arc stays visible between the floor skids.

skinChecks.note: left sole stays flat on the sled plate
right sole stays flat on the sled plate
sit bones stay on the seat pan
